material.body: Open question answerable by code: on linux/darwin/windows, does sharing one address space preserve the guest seccomp filter, hop thread, W^X, memory cap and backstop isolation?
material.subject: Can all laboon instances share one address space without a security regression?
material.witness_evidence: docs/SINGLE_ADDRESS_SPACE.md plus adversarial security recon (receipt 1794973970756-15-f63df22e16b46957): R1 no MMU boundary and WRPKRU is unprivileged, R2 PROT_R hop alias needs two page tables, R3 process-scoped seccomp/Seatbelt/LPAC kill blast radius, R4 fork COW, R5 process-global stub window, R11 process-wide accounting. Verdict: a global single address space is NOT achievable without regressions; keep one space per instance and share the supervisor control plane.
